Phoenix to Flagstaff shuttle, private and chauffeured

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Phoenix to Flagstaff shuttle: one chauffeured vehicle for your group, door to door from Phoenix, Scottsdale or Sky Harbor, and the same ride from Flagstaff to Phoenix. If checkout measures the drive at 2½ hours each way, one way is $725 before 8% tax in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) for up to 6, or $875 in an Executive Sprinter for up to 14. Questions? Call (623) 986-6339 or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

Last updated: October 6, 2026

How do you get from Phoenix to Flagstaff without driving?

Book a private chauffeured transfer: one vehicle for your group only, door to door from any Phoenix or Scottsdale address, Sky Harbor included, to your address in Flagstaff, with no shared stops and no timetable. In the Luxury SUV (Suburban), for up to 6 with 10 bags, if checkout measures the drive at 2½ hours each way, one way is $725 before 8% tax. This is not a shared shuttle. A shared van sells seats on its own schedule; a private transfer leaves when you choose, from where you are, and goes where you are staying. The whole vehicle is yours, so the price does not change with the headcount. People book the run for Northern Arizona University move-in and graduation, a ski day at Snowbowl, a cabin weekend, the start of a Grand Canyon trip, or the ride home to Sky Harbor. Every figure on this page comes from the same rate grid and pricing engine as checkout.

How far is Flagstaff from Phoenix, and how long is the drive?

From Old Town Scottsdale: about 150 miles by road to downtown Flagstaff, about 2½ to 3 hours in clear weather each way without stops or traffic delays. From Phoenix Sky Harbor: about 150 miles by road to downtown Flagstaff, about 2¼ to 2¾ hours in clear weather each way without stops or traffic delays. Your chauffeur plans the route; the checkout measures your own two addresses and prices from that drive. The road is Interstate 17 north to Flagstaff, which sits near 7,000 feet where I-17 meets I-40. In December 2025 ADOT announced the substantial completion of its I-17 Improvement Project: 15 miles of new third lanes from Anthem Way to Black Canyon City and 8 miles of flex lanes from Black Canyon City to Sunset Point. The flex lanes carry one direction at a time, ADOT says, typically northbound Monday through Saturday and southbound on Sunday, and southbound on both Sunday and Monday over long holiday weekends. Sunset Point, ADOT’s rest area between mileposts 251 and 252, sits on the southbound side but serves both directions, with a sweeping view of the Bradshaw Mountains to the west. An added stop on a transfer is $50.

What about snow on the road to Flagstaff?

Flagstaff averages about 108 inches of snow a year, Discover Flagstaff says, and ADOT counts it among the snowiest cities in the United States. Before a winter trip, check AZ511 or its app for road and weather conditions; ADOT’s advice when a storm hits and the trip is not necessary is to delay and wait it out. If a storm makes us cancel a ride, our policy treats it like any cancellation on our side: you get 100% back or a free reschedule, your choice.

Is there a Flagstaff to Phoenix shuttle for the ride back?

Yes. The chauffeur collects you at a Flagstaff home, hotel or cabin, or on the Northern Arizona University campus, for the drive down to Phoenix, Scottsdale or Sky Harbor, priced from the measured drive. Booked together with the ride up, the return comes off 20%, and the pickup time and address are set in writing before you pay. Flagstaff also has its own airport, Flagstaff Pulliam (FLG), less than a mile off I-17 at exit 337; as of October 6, 2026, the airport says American Airlines flies from it daily to Phoenix and Dallas/Fort Worth. Amtrak’s Southwest Chief stops at the station at 1 East Route 66, between downtown and the NAU campus.

Can we ride up to Arizona Snowbowl?

Snowbowl is 7 miles north of Flagstaff on US 180 and then up Snowbowl Road, which is paved and plowed; after winter storms, chains or four-wheel drive may be required, and parking is not allowed anywhere along Snowbowl Road. On chains-or-4WD days Snowbowl runs a free shuttle from Fort Valley Lodge, at the base of Snowbowl Road, for guests holding a lift ticket or season pass, so a group can be dropped at the lodge and ride up. Snow play is not allowed at Snowbowl or along its road, and Discover Flagstaff says there is no parking or stopping on Highway 180. For a ski or snow day with the vehicle waiting, the Flagstaff snow day is our hourly tour; the ride on this page is the transfer.

What else near Flagstaff suits a group?

Lowell Observatory sits on Mars Hill one mile west of historic downtown, and its visitor lot takes buses and RVs, first come, first served; as of October 6, 2026, it is closed on Tuesdays. Walnut Canyon National Monument is about 7.5 miles east of Flagstaff, by I-40 exit 204 and a 3-mile road; the Park Service recommends 40 feet as the maximum length for oversized vehicles there and warns that GPS can send drivers down Forest Road 303, a dirt road that often needs high clearance. Sunset Crater Volcano’s visitor center is 12 miles north on US 89 and then 2 miles along the Sunset Crater–Wupatki Loop Road, the Park Service says, and the Wupatki visitor center is 21 miles from that turnoff. Through October 21, 2026, Forest Road 545 is closed to all vehicles from near the highway to the park entrance kiosk by Bonito Campground, and the Park Service expects it to reopen on October 22. Meanwhile the monument, its visitor center and trails stay open, the Park Service says, reached on Forest Road 545 through Wupatki National Monument, a 19-mile, 30-minute drive between the two visitor centers; the unpaved Forest Road 776 detour is not suitable for RVs and trailers. For the Grand Canyon, the Park Service lists three ways from Flagstaff to the South Rim: I-40 west to Williams and Highway 64 north; Highway 180 to Valle and Highway 64; or Highway 89 to Cameron and Highway 64 west to the Desert View entrance. Our Grand Canyon South Rim tour is the canyon day.

Which Flagstaff dates should a group plan around?

Arizona Snowbowl’s 2026–27 season is scheduled to open on Friday, November 20, 2026, the resort says. Northern Arizona University’s fall commencement is Friday, December 11, 2026: one ceremony for all colleges, at 10 a.m. NAU’s spring commencement is May 7 and 8, 2027, at the J. Lawrence Walkup Skydome; a continuous shuttle carries guests between the university’s garage or lot P62 and the Skydome, and Uber and Lyft use the San Francisco Parking Garage (P96B). Send the reservations desk the date, the address and the arrival time you need, and the pickup is confirmed in writing.

Which vehicle should we book for Flagstaff?

Count winter coats, boots and gear along with riders. Up to 6: the Luxury SUV (Suburban), with room for 10 bags. Up to 14: an Executive Sprinter, black or white, with room for 40. Up to 29: the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), 30 bags. Up to 56: the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, 125 bags, for a team or a whole wedding party. For a small party the lowest fare on this page is the Luxury SUV (Suburban)’s; the Maybach Jet Sprinter seats 9, four of them massage and reclining seats in Maybach leather, with room for 4 checked bags.

Can we go to Flagstaff and back in one day?

Yes. Hire the vehicle for the day and it waits in Flagstaff while you ski, hike or visit the observatory: ten hours costs $1,305 in an Executive Sprinter and $1,125 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), before tax. Free hours apply from 7 booked hours, so a ten-hour day is billed as 9 hours.

What does the Flagstaff fare include?

Included: your chauffeur, fuel and bottled water. Added at checkout: 8% Arizona sales tax; there is no booking fee, service charge or fuel surcharge. Gratuity is up to you, and the deposit, balance and cancellation terms are on our policies page. Arizona law lets passengers aged 21 or older bring their own drinks aboard a for-hire vehicle, but if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on the trip; the chauffeur never drinks, and there is no smoking or vaping on board.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a shuttle cost from Phoenix to Flagstaff?

A transfer for the whole vehicle: $725 one way before tax in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), which takes up to 6 riders, or $875 in a 14-seat Executive Sprinter, at 2½ hours each way; your exact total comes from your own addresses at checkout.

Is there an airport shuttle from Phoenix Sky Harbor to Flagstaff?

Yes, a private pickup at your terminal. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit. Add the airline and flight number to the booking; your confirmation names the pickup method and meeting point, and the chauffeur sends the pickup instruction once you land.

Is there a Phoenix to Flagstaff shuttle schedule?

No. There is no timetable to fit: you pick the day and the pickup time, the vehicle leaves from your address, and the price is for the vehicle, not per seat.

Is there a shuttle from Flagstaff to Phoenix Sky Harbor?

Yes, private and door to door: from your Flagstaff address to your Sky Harbor terminal, priced from the measured drive and set in writing before you pay.

Can you drive us up to Arizona Snowbowl in winter?

As far as the road allows that day. After storms, Snowbowl Road may require chains or four-wheel drive, and on those days Snowbowl’s free shuttle runs from Fort Valley Lodge at the bottom of the road for guests with a lift ticket or season pass.

Does Flagstaff have its own airport?

Yes: Flagstaff Pulliam Airport (FLG), at 6200 S. Pulliam Drive, less than a mile off I-17 at exit 337. As of October 6, 2026, the airport says American Airlines flies from it to Phoenix and Dallas/Fort Worth.
